security_audit.summary: The skill appears to be a legitimate Jira Cloud integration, and most Markdown backtick detections are false positives from examples and inline documentation. I confirmed intended network and environment access in the helper script, plus one high-risk .env loading issue because it reads from the current working directory. No prompt injection or covert exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Only load JIRA_DOMAIN, JIRA_EMAIL, and JIRA_API_TOKEN from an explicit config file, or require an opt-in flag before reading .env.
Prefer the helper script for authentication and replace manual base64 curl examples with safer guidance that avoids token exposure.
Validate that JIRA_DOMAIN points to an expected Atlassian host unless the user explicitly allows a custom Jira domain.
Update SKILL.md examples to match scripts/jira-api.py, or rename the helper so users do not edit commands incorrectly.

content.user_title: Manage Jira Issues from Your AI Agent
content.value_statement: Jira work often requires repeated searches, updates, and status changes across tickets. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical Jira Cloud workflows with REST API and JQL guidance.
actual_capabilities: Search Jira issues with JQL patterns and REST API v3 endpoints.
Retrieve issue details, project metadata, available transitions, and issue types.
Create and update issues using Atlassian Document Format guidance.
Add comments, change issue status, assign users, and unassign issues.
Use a Python helper script for authenticated Jira Cloud API requests.
Reference Jira API, JQL, and ADF documentation included with the skill.
limitations: Requires Jira Cloud credentials and a valid API token from the user.
Does not manage OAuth flows or Jira Server authentication.
Documentation examples reference scripts/jira_api.py, while the bundled file is scripts/jira-api.py.
Successful writes depend on the Jira user permissions and project field configuration.

use_cases.title: Triage sprint work
use_cases.description: Search open sprint issues, review status, and identify tickets that need updates or reassignment.

use_cases.title: Create implementation tickets
use_cases.description: Turn product requirements into Jira tasks with structured descriptions, labels, and issue metadata.

use_cases.title: Automate support follow-up
use_cases.description: Find recent customer issues, add clear comments, and move tickets through configured workflow transitions.

prompt_templates.title: Find my open work
prompt_templates.prompt: Find my unresolved Jira issues updated in the last seven days. Summarize each issue key, status, assignee, and next action.

prompt_templates.title: Create a task
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Jira task in project PROJ for this requirement: [requirement]. Include a concise summary, clear description, and useful labels.

prompt_templates.title: Update a ticket
prompt_templates.prompt: Update PROJ-123 with this new summary and comment: [details]. Preserve existing context and use Jira-compatible rich text.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a release queue
prompt_templates.prompt: Search release-blocking issues for version [version], group them by status and owner, then propose safe transition or comment updates for each issue.

output_examples.input: Show my unresolved Jira issues from this sprint.
output: PROJ-142: Payment retry fails in staging. Status: In Progress. Next action: confirm latest test result.
PROJ-155: Update onboarding copy. Status: To Do. Next action: assign owner before sprint review.

output_examples.input: Create a task for adding audit logs to admin exports.
output_examples.output: Created PROJ-482 with a concise task summary, structured description, and audit, admin, and backend labels.

output_examples.input: Move PROJ-123 forward if a Ready for QA transition exists.
output_examples.output: Found the Ready for QA transition, applied it, and added a short comment with the verification context.

best_practices: Confirm project keys, issue types, and required fields before creating issues.
Use narrow JQL filters to avoid large result sets and rate limits.
Review write operations before applying comments, assignments, or transitions.
anti_patterns: Do not store Jira API tokens in shared repositories or committed files.
Do not run broad searches when a project, sprint, or issue key is known.
Do not transition issues without checking available workflow transitions first.

faq.question: Does this skill work with Jira Cloud?
faq.answer: Yes. It targets Jira Cloud REST API v3 and uses Jira Cloud API tokens.

faq.question: Does it support Jira Server or Data Center?
faq.answer: No. The included guidance and helper script are written for Jira Cloud endpoints.

faq.question: Can it create and update issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes workflows for issue creation, field updates, comments, assignments, and transitions.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: Users need a Jira domain, Jira account email, and Jira API token with suitable permissions.

faq.question: Can it help write JQL?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes common JQL patterns and a reference file for fields, operators, and functions.

faq.question: Does it automatically validate Jira permissions?
faq.answer: No. Jira returns permission and field errors, and users must resolve them in their Jira configuration.
